clean_summary:
Continual learning agents with finite capacity face the challenge of balancing the acquisition of new knowledge while retaining old knowledge. This necessitates controlled forgetting of information that is no longer needed, which helps free up capacity for new learning.

The paper explores weight decay as a mechanism to facilitate this controlled forgetting. By adapting weight decay, the model can prioritize which knowledge to retain and which to forget, ultimately improving the efficiency of continual learning processes.

summary:
Sora 2 is out!
I'm incredibly impressed that despite Sora 1 setting a ridiculous bar — as the largest jump in video capability basically ever — Sora 2 somehow matches up here.
For people that played around a lot with Sora 1, it didn't feel clear that Sora really 'understood' the world, or physics, (and definitely not counting). Sora 2 is intelligent in a way we haven't seen with a video model before — and that's a combination of so many incredible breakthroughs here stacked together.
As a personal curiosity, I've spent a lot of time talking to people in robotics, self-driving, drones, etc. over the last year. Every single one of them told me one thing: that the limit to perfect performance was perfect simulators for RL. Video models like Sora 2, as both a simulator or a policy, have the potential to be revolutionary.
Of course, I’m still very concerned about how video models will end up affecting the world’s information ecosystem, politics and regimes, or people’s mental health. Video models are clearly dual-use: I’m very optimistic that the benefits we’ll see from embodied intelligence and the physical world will be enormous, and that society and our technology platforms will adapt to respond to synthetic media (and I also won't mind seeing all the incredible content people will use this technology to create).
Congrats to the whole Sora team on all the great work! The team continues to prove itself as one of the best research teams in the world. @model_mechanic and @billpeeb are the GOATs
